transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 16:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Partner Ops); Marta, Ethan, Samir, Lena, Tom (Calyx)
Shared artifacts: co-sell-playbook-v1.pdf (link), benchmark-template.xlsx (link), security-zip (link)

Summary (auto):
Quick-run co-sell alignment workshop with Calyx to decide go/no-go for a pilot. Covered economics split, proof-of-value criteria, security gating (SOC 2 / SSO / KMS), and data flow for VPC/private deployment. Agreed next steps: Redwood sends economics 1-pager, Calyx provides traffic samples, schedule infra benchmark in early Dec.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: All right hey everyone, thanks for being flexible, I know this landed on a Tuesday afternoon. Quick roll call then we'll jump in — Ava from Redwood here, Jonah with me —
[00:08] Jonah Lee: hi hi, Jonah SE — gonna run the benchmark plan portion after we align on the co-sell mechanics.
[00:13] Marta Vega: Marta here, hi. Ethan, Samir, Lena, Tom also on. Looks like we have the playbook link, thanks.
[00:21] Ava Martinez: Great. Goal for today is pragmatic — decide if we can run a 6-week pilot with the partner motion, see what success looks like, and surface any fatal security or procurement objections early.
[00:31] Tom Brooks (Calyx): From partner side we want clarity on revenue splits and lead routing. If Calyx introduces a customer through our partner network, how do we share credit and what incentives does Redwood give the partner?
[00:44] Priya Rao: We have a couple of default co-sell templates we use, Tom — we'll send examples. Generally there are two patterns: referral fee vs. joint-sale carve. We can be flexible on carve based on committed revenue.
[00:56] Ethan Ross: Also timeline constraints — we have a Q1 customer launch that's driving the urgency. If pilot runs into Jan we need a fast path from pilot -> go-live.
[01:06] Ava Martinez: Understood. Jonas — sorry Jonah — can you run through the pilot profile we think best demonstrates value?
[01:13] Jonah Lee: Sure. Proposed pilot: 4 weeks of live traffic replay plus a 2-week canary on production traffic with conservative throttles. Focus on three endpoints: clinical note summarization, triage classifier, and embeddings for search. We want to show latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and correctness vs current baseline.
[01:33] Marta Vega: Are you expecting us to send raw PHI? Data residency is a concern.
[01:37] Jonah Lee: We do not need PHI for the initial run — replay can be de-identified or synthetic. For the production canary we'd need contract language and DPA, plus KMS integration if you want Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private.
[01:50] Lena Hu: On the security front we need SOC 2 Type II, proof of encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, and SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. Also audit trail retention for 12 months.
[02:03] Ava Martinez: That's in line with what our Private deployments support — we can do customer KMS, and audit logs via the console. We'll attach our SOC 2 cert and the security questionnaire.
[02:13] Samir Patel: Procurement question — what's the minimum contract term for Dedicated vs hosted pilot? Our procurement team balks at long lock-ins.
[02:21] Priya Rao: For pilots we typically do a 3-month pilot contract with option to convert to monthly committed after go-live. Dedicated reservations are annual but we can structure a limited reserved pilot with a conversion credit.
[02:33] Tom Brooks: How would revenue recognition / partner commission work if we convert mid-term? Partners need clear math - will they get uplift if they introduced the customer?
[02:41] Ava Martinez: We usually implement a time-limited referral fee for 12 months on usage, or a one-time reseller commission. We can provide concrete examples in the 1-pager.
[02:51] Ethan Ross: Technical: latency targets are strict — many of our users expect sub-300ms on the summarization endpoint. Can Redwood hit that with a hosted model?
[03:02] Jonah Lee: Depends on model variant and sequence length. With our optimized attention kernels and continuous batching we can get sub-300ms p50 on a tflite-quantized model for 512 tokens in hosted regions close to your users. For guaranteed p95 you'd want Dedicated or Private with pinned capacity. There's always a tradeoff between cost and latency.
[03:22] Marta Vega: What about multiregion routing — some of our customers are EU-only.
[03:27] Ava Martinez: We support region routing policy — requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region). For EU-only you'll likely want Redwood Private in an EU VPC or our hosted EU region with data residency guarantees.
[03:37] Tom Brooks: Pricing splits matter — if we do referral fee, do you share net revenue after credits or gross? We need to see an example.
[03:45] Priya Rao: We'll send examples. Typically it's net usage after standard credits; also you can elect to include partner margin in pricing and adjust commissions accordingly.
[03:55] Lena Hu: Quick technical security clarif: for customer-managed keys, do we support HSM-backed KMS? And how is key escrow handled?
[04:03] Jonah Lee: Yes, we support HSM-backed KMS — in Redwood Private you bring your own key and we use it for disk + object encryption. For Hosted we offer integration with major cloud KMS providers; we do not hold the key material for Private options. Key escrow policies can be written into the SOW.
[04:19] Ethan Ross: Can we get a short example flow diagram for data? I'd like to show infra what goes where.
[04:24] Ava Martinez: We'll attach an architecture diagram to the follow-up. It will show inference in Dedicated pool, VPC peering, egress controls, and audit log sink.
[04:33] Marta Vega: Regarding benchmarks, Jonah, you mentioned cost per 1k tokens. Can you show us the variables and how caching affects that?
[04:40] Jonah Lee: Absolutely. For summarization workloads caching prefix tokens or KV cache hits reduce per-token decode cost — we'll show simulated numbers with and without prefix cache in the benchmark template. Also batching impacts latency/cost tradeoff — we'll propose a batching policy that keeps the 95th under a target while improving throughput.
[04:57] Samir Patel: Procurement will need an outline of liability and indemnity for partner-led deals. Is that standard?
[05:02] Priya Rao: We have partner-language in our master services agreement. We can surface a redline view with partner carve clauses after the economics are agreed.
[05:12] Tom Brooks: Hypothetical: Calyx brings Acme Health in through partner channel. They want a co-sell where we both demo and split rev 70/30. If Redwood's unit economics are tight at our target pricepoint, how much flexibility do you have?
[05:27] Ava Martinez: We can be flexible especially for large-volume commitments — we usually map revenue splits to uplift delivered and commit tiers. We'll include a few scenarios (small pilot, mid-market, enterprise) in the 1-pager.
[05:40] Ethan Ross: On instrumentation — we need token-level cost breakdowns and tracing hooks to correlate latency spikes to model versions. Do you expose model-level traces?
[05:50] Jonah Lee: Yes. Redwood Console exposes per-model/per-route dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We can also integrate with your existing observability via exporter.
[06:05] Marta Vega: Are there known gotchas for models with long KV caches? We use long-context notes at times.
[06:11] Jonah Lee: Long KV cache increases memory pressure and may push you to larger instance classes. We recommend hybrid strategies: prefix pruning + LRU cache and quantization profiles. We also offer recommended quant configs by workload in Redwood Optimize.
[06:29] Tom Brooks: Can partners resell Dedicated capacity? We have channel partners that prefer reselling committed pools.
[06:35] Priya Rao: Yes, we can do reseller carveouts on Dedicated; resale programs require partner onboarding and a reseller agreement. We'll cover the onboarding timeline in the playbook.
[06:45] Lena Hu: One more security concern: access controls for partner users — we need strict RBAC to avoid partner visibility into unrelated customers.
[06:53] Jonah Lee: RBAC is supported — role-based permissions, org-scoped teams, and route-level permissions. We can lock partner views to only their accounts.
[07:03] Ava Martinez: Good. Let's talk failure modes — if Dedicated capacity saturates, do we automatically burst to hosted?
[07:11] Jonah Lee: We have automatic fallback policies: route-level policies can prefer Dedicated, then fall back to hosted compatible model variants if capacity is constrained. That's often how we keep SLAs during peak traffic.
[07:22] Marta Vega: Does fallback change token billing? We need to understand billing implications if a request falls back to a different model variant.
[07:29] Ava Martinez: Billing follows the runtime used — we'll show a billing scenario sheet. For co-sell deals we can also build in credits for fallback usage during a grace period.
[07:40] Samir Patel: Who signs the SOW if this is a partner-introduced deal — Redwood + Calyx + End Customer or Redwood + End Customer with Calyx as reseller?
[07:48] Priya Rao: Both models are possible. Typically reseller is Redwood-EndCustomer with partner as reseller on the order form. Joint sale can be a tripartite SOW; we'll surface pros/cons.
[07:58] Tom Brooks: We need to lock down a pilot start window. Could we aim to start data replay the week of Dec 14?
[08:04] Ava Martinez: That works for Redwood; Jonah, is that feasible for benchmarks and infra prep?
[08:09] Jonah Lee: Yes — we'll need traffic samples by Dec 2 and a runbook, then we'll provision a sandbox Dedicated pool and schedule a smoke test the week prior.
[08:18] Marta Vega: I'll coordinate with our infra folks and send the sample traffic and an allowlist for IPs.
[08:23] Lena Hu: I'll also share the security questionnaire answers. A heads up — our legal will want a liability cap in line with our SOC 2 controls.
[08:31] Ava Martinez: Noted. We'll propose standard language and highlight where exceptions may be needed.
[08:38] Ethan Ross: Real quick on performance numbers — can you share a previous benchmark from another healthcare customer? Even an anonymized table would help us baseline expectations.
[08:46] Jonah Lee: I can share an anonymized benchmark showing p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens for summarize/embeddings. Will scrub customer names.
[08:53] Tom Brooks: From partner ops angle — what's the partner enablement timeline? We need training and co-marketing assets.
[08:59] Priya Rao: We have a 2-week enablement bundle: training session, sales play deck, technical handoff doc, and a co-branded landing page template. We'll plan the enablement to overlap with the pilot's second week so partners can start outreach during the canary.
[09:14] Marta Vega: One more question: latency SLA. If we put SLA into the contract, what are typical credits?
[09:21] Ava Martinez: SLA credits vary by deployment — hosted has best-effort, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll propose SLA language in the SOW options appendix.
[09:33] Samir Patel: Are there any upfront engineering fees for the private/VPC option?
[09:38] Priya Rao: Sometimes we charge a one-time onboarding fee for on-prem or private deployments to cover network design and security hardening. We'll list both options in the 1-pager.
[09:47] Tom Brooks: Ok this has been helpful. Can we recap next steps quickly?
[09:51] Ava Martinez: Sure. Recap: Redwood to send co-sell economics 1-pager + sample contract language (Ava), Jonah to send benchmark plan and anonymized healthcare benchmark (Jonah), Calyx to share traffic samples and security questionnaire (Marta and Lena), Procurement touchpoint Samir to confirm contract term preferences. Schedule infra benchmark for week of Dec 14.
[10:14] Marta Vega: Confirmed. I'll get the samples to you by Dec 2.
[10:18] Lena Hu: Security questionnaire by Friday (2026-11-27).
[10:22] Tom Brooks: Partners will review commission targets and come back to you by 2026-11-30.
[10:27] Ava Martinez: Great — we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
[10:31] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears for acronyms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash) and product names (Redwood Dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated).
